issues.description: compile_notebook RPC ships full script content in every response instead of exposing on-demand download.
issues.detail: The compile response now embeds arbitrary-size file contents as a side product of compilation, bloating every call for a button that's only sometimes used and silently broadening the RPC contract. Add a dedicated read_script(path) or download RPC the frontend invokes on click, keeping the compile envelope small and the contract explicit.

issues.description: open() on the compiled script lacks encoding and error handling, so a post-success read failure fails the whole compile.
issues.detail: open(script_path) uses the platform default encoding and is unguarded. If the file is missing, unreadable, or non-utf8 on the server's locale, the RPC reports compile failure even though compilation succeeded. Specify encoding='utf-8' and wrap the read so a download-side problem cannot poison the compile result.

issues.description: Download icon renders unconditionally while the click handler guards on compiledContent, producing silent no-op clicks.
issues.detail: handleDownloadClick early-returns when compiledContent is absent (older backend, partial response, error paths), but the icon still renders in the success branch with no disabled state or feedback. Either gate rendering on compiledContent being present or render a disabled affordance so users get a clear signal instead of a dead click.

issues.description: DeployProgress conflates progress rendering with file-download mechanics.
issues.detail: handleDownloadClick embeds Blob construction, object URL creation, DOM anchor manipulation, and revoke lifecycle inside a component whose job is to render state. Extract a downloadFile(name, content) utility so the component stays a pure renderer and the download mechanism is substitutable and testable on its own.

issues.description: Duplicate compiledPath and compiledContent state is prop-drilled through four files when one would suffice.
issues.detail: compiledPath is used only to derive a filename via split('/').pop(), while compiledContent carries the bytes. Carrying both through DeployProgressState, DeploysProgress, DeployProgress, and Commands is unnecessary plumbing — return a filename plus content, or keep the path and fetch on click. Also document the field's lifetime invariant where it's declared.

issues.description: GetAppIcon used as a click target instead of a real button, harming accessibility.
issues.detail: It's an SVG icon with onClick and a title attr — no keyboard handler, no role, no focus ring. The adjacent 'Done' affordance is an anchor for exactly this reason. Wrap in IconButton or use an <a download> with an object URL so the control is focusable, keyboard-activatable, and matches the surrounding code's style.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the download feature is reasonable but the shape is wrong. The compile_notebook RPC silently broadened its contract to ship arbitrary-size file contents on every call, and the read uses the platform default encoding with no error handling — so a post-success read failure poisons the compile result. On the frontend, the download icon renders without gating on compiledContent (silent no-op clicks), uses an SVG instead of a real button, and DeployProgress conflates progress rendering with browser download mechanics. The fix is to expose a dedicated download/read-script RPC, specify encoding, extract a download utility, and tighten the precondition on rendering the affordance.
